samples.summary: The delta's real new logic — YorkieStore.setMerge budgeting, refusal, and the batchMerges/projectedMerges overlay — has no test anywhere
samples.evidence: This delta rewrites YorkieStore.setMerge to (a) spend the merge budget at call time against a projected map, (b) exclude the anchor's own existing span when re-anchoring, (c) return false on refusal, and (d) track queued writes in `batchMerges` so a paste's many blocks are budgeted against the map the batch is building. No test exercises any of it: grep for `setMerge|projectedMerges|batchMerges` matches no file under packages/frontend/tests (only src + sheets tests), and a case-insensitive grep for `merge` across packages/frontend/tests returns only docs/slides/utils tests. The sheets tests added here use MemStore subclasses whose setMerge is overridden wholesale, so they never touch the budget arithmetic. If the overlay or the self-exclusion is wrong, a paste can overspend the cap (storing a merge map a later load cannot walk) or silently drop a legal re-anchor — both data-affecting and invisible to the green suite.

samples.summary: No test covers the new refusal handling on the move/cut-paste merge path
samples.evidence: The delta adds `if (!(await this.store.setMerge(anchor, merge.span))) continue;` to the movedMerges loop, but merge.test.ts's new RefusingStore/ToggleRefusingStore tests only cover mergeSelection and a plain paste. The existing 'should drop a cut merged block at the source' test uses a plain MemStore that always accepts, so the new `continue` branch is never executed. If it regresses, this.merges records a block the store does not hold — in-memory drift that renders a phantom merge until reload.

samples.summary: Batched deleteMerge now consults the projected map instead of the document; no test covers delete-after-set-within-one-batch
samples.evidence: deleteMerge's batch branch changed from `!!ws.merges?.[sref]` to `this.projectedMerges().has(sref)` and now records `batchMerges.set(sref, null)`. That makes deleting a block queued earlier in the same batch return true (previously false) and frees its budget for later blocks in the batch. No test in packages/frontend/tests touches YorkieStore merges at all, so this reachability change ships unverified; a mistake here mis-budgets a paste or returns a wrong boolean to the engine.

setMerge in ReadOnlyStore changed from a void no-op to returning false, which now makes Sheet.mergeSelection return false against a read-only store. packages/sheets/test/store/store.test.ts contains no occurrence of 'Merge', and no other test constructs a Sheet over ReadOnlyStore to assert merge behavior. Low impact (read-only path already refuses edits), but the contract change is uncovered.

verdict.reason: The behavior exists exactly as described: YorkieStore.projectedMerges() (yorkie-store.ts:975-991) overlays batchMerges (declared :85, initialized in beginBatch :1232, cleared in endBatch :1240) on the document merge map, and setMerge (:1008-1040) spends mergeBudgetAdmits/mergeBudgetOf against that projection while excluding the anchor's own existing span, returning false on refusal. I could find no test exercising any of it. Repo-wide grep for setMerge|projectedMerges|batchMerges matches only sheets/cli/backend tests, none of which build a YorkieStore; repo-wide grep for YorkieStore shows only three frontend tests (yorkie-axis-order, yorkie-store-read-only, yorkie-cut-paste) plus helpers, and a case-insensitive 'merge' grep over all frontend test files hits nothing in them (the only spreadsheet hit, remote-change-utils.test.ts:17-18, just asserts on the change-path string "$.sheets.tab-1.merges.0"). yorkie-cut-paste.test.ts is the only test that drives beginBatch/endBatch on a real store and it only uses setGrid/delete/get — and is skipped unless YORKIE_RPC_ADDR is set. Coverage by proxy is also absent: MemStore.setMerge (packages/sheets/src/store/memory.ts:586-589) contains no budget arithmetic at all, and packages/sheets/test/sheet/merge.test.ts only tests the mergeBudget* helpers in isolation (:17-51) and Sheet's reaction to a subclass that hardcodes a refusal (:475-511). So the refusal path, the re-anchor self-exclusion, and the batch overlay have no meaningful test; if any is wrong a paste can overspend the entry/covered-cell cap (persisting a merge map a later load cannot walk) or silently drop a legal re-anchor — silent and data-affecting, hence major under the test-adequacy rubric.
